feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid public-sector specialization. It is well written overall, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, and could sharpen impact by foregrounding outcomes more consistently.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, culminating in leadership roles with strong scope, ownership, and technical breadth.  
- Good use of scale indicators and specifics (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers), which boosts credibility.  
- Writing is polished and professional, with a strong strategic positioning in the header and relevant project examples.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across sections: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused evidence beyond responsibilities, especially for consulting and earlier roles: quantify improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, or campaign performance where possible.  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation in lists is inconsistent (e.g., “social, and multimedia” vs. “web, email, social and video”); “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak filler. No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It’s slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets; tightening it will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Make the opening more specific and active: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years…” reads more directly than “Senior digital leader…”
- Add scale or context from recent roles to sharpen credibility, e.g., “enterprise web modernization for 10,000+ page public-sector sites” or “high-volume member communications.”
- Trim the long capability list; group related areas to improve flow and avoid sounding like a skills section.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web, analytics, and editorial systems for high-volume public-sector organizations. Leads digital governance, content operations, multimedia production, and AI-enabled user experiences that improve discovery, publishing efficiency, and audience engagement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “AI-enabled user experiences” is useful, but avoid repeating it elsewhere in the header/subtitle.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize distinctive capability areas rather than repeating broad phrases already covered elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, sharper competency labels for faster scanning and cleaner visual rhythm.
- Replace “communications operations” with more specific leadership language, e.g., “multi-channel content operations” or “digital channel leadership.”
- Consider this tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel content and campaign operations • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream delivery
- Keep style consistent by avoiding mixed constructions like “systems,” “operations,” and “experiences” unless each adds distinct meaning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” are already strongly covered in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” also repeats positioning already established in the header and work history.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use stronger, more specific verbs and simplify phrasing: e.g., “Created an AI-powered legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content, and bill-level chat.”
- Standardize style and punctuation across entries; “10×20-foot” is fine, but keep all items in the same sentence structure.
- Where possible, add light outcome/context signals without duplicating metrics from Experience, such as audience, campaign purpose, or organizational use.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with recent NACo roles; keep this section project-focused, not responsibility-focused.
- “Built” and “Developed” repeat heavily; vary verbs to avoid sounding formulaic.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten around consultant-level impact, transformation, and only the newest/highest-value work.

Suggested edit:
- Open with outcome + scope: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancement, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for enterprise communications.”
- Replace generic verbs (“consult,” “build and refine,” “deliver”) with sharper impact language: “modernized,” “streamlined,” “architected,” “launched,” “optimized.”
- Consolidate into 3–4 bullets, e.g.:
- Architect digital workflows, analytics, and governance improvements supporting coordinated cross-channel communications.
- Build Drupal campaign experiences, including microsites, modular content components, and member-facing resource hubs.
- Lead AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery experience.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, publishing time reduced, engagement gains, search success, or toolkit downloads.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this item focused on consulting impact and new initiatives.
- Microsite and AI search details also appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same examples verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget across enterprise platforms.”
- Combine and tighten web modernization: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership outcome-focused: replace “reaching tens of thousands…” with a metric on growth, engagement, deliverability, or campaign performance if available.
- Strengthen impact language: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal production capacity for advocacy, events and recurring multimedia content”; “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery reporting to improve leadership visibility and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video/programming language also appears in older NACo roles; emphasize studio build-out and operational scale here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry is too close to the adjacent NACo roles and relies on “helped” language that weakens ownership. Tighten it around operational leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth to show clear step-up before the director role.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize ownership: “Led NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media, and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging.”
- Replace weaker bullets with action + outcome framing: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Strengthen the video bullet: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper line: “Built stronger editorial planning and cross-team publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams, improving consistency and execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; keep this version focused on scaling/operationalizing it.
- “Publishing workflows” and “coordination” also appear in the 2022–2024 role; avoid repeating governance language too heavily.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should be tightened to emphasize senior-level scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad labels with sharper, differentiated language tied to enterprise leadership:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel communications operations” to align with recent experience and avoid vague leadership wording.
- Use “audience-centered” or “user-centered” instead of “audience-focused” for a more current, strategic tone.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable scale (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) for work experience rather than skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” repeat the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution themes rather than exhaustive technologies.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- Cut lower-signal items if space is tight; “WordPress” may matter less than enterprise modernization unless target roles explicitly want it.
- If possible, tie to scale elsewhere in the CV, e.g., “Drupal modernization for 10,000+ page public-sector sites” rather than listing platforms alone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies and the header summary.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the recent NACo leadership roles, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. Make this more outcome-oriented and leadership-level.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics Strategy, Reporting & Optimization**
- Replace the list with grouped, higher-value phrasing: **GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership reporting • SEO, UX and performance analysis**
- Consider adding one impact cue if space allows: **Built analytics infrastructure to support strategic decision-making across high-traffic public-sector web properties**
- Keep this section focused on strategic application; leave pure tool inventory to Technical + IT

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates **Technical + IT → Data, Analytics & Optimization**; avoid repeating the same tools in both places.
- “Leadership reporting” may overlap with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies; use one for strategy, the other for systems.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. Make it more senior, systems-oriented, and tied to recent in-house studio/event leadership rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Systems & Event Production**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level bullets such as:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production  
- Livestream and hybrid event production  
- In-house studio buildout and operations  
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows
- If space allows, make one item more strategic: **Recurring advocacy video programming and event delivery**
- Keep phrasing parallel and outcome-oriented; avoid entry-level wording like “video editing” unless paired with broader ownership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; use this section for more specific execution strengths.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “livestreaming”; combine rather than listing both separately.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add level/context or be tightened to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider signaling depth: **Drupal (enterprise modernization, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add proficiency framing rather than just names: **Enterprise CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages; static publishing via GitHub Pages**
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** if it’s not materially used in recent roles; it reads lighter than the rest.
- Keep terminology consistent with the CV’s leadership tone: use **CMS platforms** or **Web platforms** rather than a generic tool list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**.
- Drupal already appears repeatedly in recent experience; avoid overemphasizing it in multiple sections unless adding distinct context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from broad coding languages to applied implementation: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group by function for clarity: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- Keep only tools you actively used in recent roles/projects; if possible add specificity elsewhere in CV (e.g., GTM for analytics tagging, Workers for edge logic/prototyping)
- Suggested rewrite: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- “API integrations” and technical execution themes also overlap with Core Competencies; this section should stay tool-focused, not strategic.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize categories and strongest tools first: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello | Collaboration: Slack • Microsoft Teams | Legacy/project use: Basecamp”
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses to show applied use: “Airtable (content ops databases), Power Automate/Zapier (cross-platform automation), Jira/Asana/Trello (project workflow management).”
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Project Systems” to better match your leadership profile.
- Drop weaker/older tools if space is tight; Basecamp feels least important relative to recent enterprise work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams are generic collaboration tools and may add little unless you need keyword coverage.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement capability. Since recent roles already emphasize email leadership, this item should stay concise and platform-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one qualifier to show level of use without repeating work history, e.g. **enterprise email automation**, **newsletter operations**, or **member communications**
- Example rewrite: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (enterprise email automation, newsletter and member engagement workflows)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding outcomes like newsletter reach or campaign leadership here; those are already covered in recent NACo roles.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications elsewhere, so keep this item limited to email/member platforms.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and repeats analytics platforms already evidenced in the recent Director role. Tighten it to emphasize optimization capability, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Reporting & Optimization**
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • KPI design • Dashboarding • SEO/performance analysis**
- Replace **A/B testing** unless you can support it with a concrete example elsewhere; if true, consider **Experimentation / A/B testing**.
- Consider ordering by strategic value: data collection/behavior tools first, then warehousing/reporting, then optimization skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to **Topline Skills [3] Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; either consolidate or make one more strategic and this one more tool-focused.
- “Dashboarding” and “reporting infrastructure” are already implied in recent NACo bullets, so avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and, if possible, add scale or output metrics to show early impact.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize promotion, team-building, and concrete delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Split execution from leadership: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- Replace “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows” with specifics: volume of videos/livestreams, audience reach, engagement lift, production turnaround, or process improvements.
- Tighten the closing: “Provided day-to-day supervision and production guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or early-building that program.
- Avoid repeating broad channel coverage already stated more strongly in later NACo entries.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads generic and underplays impact. Since later NACo roles already cover digital leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/research support plus the “first podcast” achievement.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the distinctive outcome: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research coordination and digital content development; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “supporting organizational programs and policy work” with clearer scope: county innovation initiatives, policy communications, research projects, stakeholder-facing materials.
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or types/volume of multimedia assets produced.
- Keep it to one concise bullet or sentence so it doesn’t compete with stronger later digital roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; avoid repeating broad multimedia language.
- Podcast/video production themes recur later, so position this as the first/launch milestone rather than ongoing channel leadership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful skill list, but it reads more like mixed capabilities than “tools,” and several items overlap with stronger, more recent experience bullets and Topline Skills. Tightening it to software/platforms will make it cleaner and less repetitive.

Suggested edit
- Rename or refocus to emphasize tools only: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator”
- If you want to keep production capabilities, separate them from software: “Video/audio editing • Livestream studio operations • Podcast production”
- Consider a stronger rewrite: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Broadcast/livestream studio operations • Podcast production workflows”
